name: Routing through trade-diversion or transshipment hubs
description: Goods or payments route through third-country hubs or ports with no commercial rationale, or hubs known for rerouting.
fp: Major hubs are used legitimately for logistics efficiency.

sources.text: FATF, Guidance for a Risk-Based Approach (sector-specific guidance series, general principles)
FATF Recommendations, Recommendation 1 and Interpretive Note (assessing risks and applying a risk-based approach)
Wolfsberg Group, Guidance on a Risk Based Approach for Managing Money Laundering Risks (2006)
FATF and Egmont Group, Trade-Based Money Laundering: Trends and Developments (2020)
ICC, BAFT and Wolfsberg Group, Trade Finance Principles (2019 update)
FATF, Guidance on Counter Proliferation Financing (2018)
FATF, Guidance on Proliferation Financing Risk Assessment and Mitigation (2021)
FATF/Egmont, Trade-Based Money Laundering: Trends and Developments (2020)

links.name: Trade-diversion or transshipment hub
links.ctx: Flows or goods route through hubs commonly used to reroute goods or avoid restrictions.
links.fp: Hubs handle huge volumes of legitimate trade.

links.name: Shipping route illogical or via high-risk transshipment
links.ctx: Goods travel through jurisdictions with no commercial reason or known risk of trade abuse.
links.fp: Route changes follow port congestion or carrier network design.

links.name: Routing via transshipment hubs unconnected to buyer or seller
links.ctx: Goods travel through third-country ports with no commercial need and are reloaded or relabelled.
links.fp: Hubs are efficient routes for many legitimate exporters.
